To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrical properties of the devices fabricated at different gravity conditions are dependent upon temperature and humidity, which is attributed to the variation of dielectric properties of the channel materials.
the humidity- and temperature-dependent properties of the OFETs are affected by the gravity condition during fabrication.

OFETs fabricated from OD and its composite with sucrose using a drop-casting method at negative gravity conditions are more humidity and heat sensitive than those fabricated at normal gravity conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fabrication of OFETs using OD and its composite with a sugar, which is a cheap and readily available organic material, and their electrical properties under different humidity and temperature conditions.
the fabrication of a new humidity and temperature sensing device based on the OD material and its composite with the sugar.
the fabrication of a humidity and temperature sensing device using a drop-casting technique at different gravity conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of OFETs fabricated using OD and OD:sugar at −1g, the capacitance–temperature relationship was more pronounced than that of impedance–humidity relationship, whereas, in the case OFETs fabricated with OD and OD:suger at +1g, the impedance–humidity relationship was more pronounced.
OFETs fabricated using OD:sugar at negative gravity (i.e., under microgravity conditions) offer higher sensitivity to temperature and humidity than those fabricated under positive gravity.
the humidity and temperature sensitivity of OFETs can be enhanced by fabricating devices at −1g and by employing OD:sugar as the channel material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of OD-based OFETs, the humidity sensitivity is higher for the devices fabricated at −1 g than those fabricated at the normal gravity (+1 g).
the OFETs fabricated using the OD:sugar at negative gravity (at −1g) have the potential for use as a humidity sensor.
, in order to achieve better performance of the OFETs, one should use the drop-casting technique at negative gravity and use OD:sugar solution as the channel definition material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the humidity and temperature sensitivity of the fabricated devices can be tuned using different solution compositions and gravity.
the fabrication of organic transistors using the drop-casting technique at negative gravity can be used to fabricate humidity and temperature sensors.
the OFETs fabricated using the drop-casting technique can be used to sense humidity and temperature.
